item.title: Los Angeles and Bay Area voters will decide whether to hike already high sales taxes
item.description: San Franciscans will consider a percentage point increase in the sales tax while Bay Area and LA-area voters will be asked for a half a percentage point.

item.title: These public documents are hidden from view. Two California lawmakers want to change that
item.description: The letters lobbyists submit to the Legislature are public documents, but they are hidden from view. Two California lawmakers want to change that

item.title: She directed $2.7 million from her elderly clients to her husband’s company. The judge approved every penny
item.description: California lawmakers created the Professional Fiduciaries Bureau to monitor self-dealing in the industry. Twenty years later, the bureau’s inaction in one case shows how conflicts of interest can continue for years with little consequence.

item.title: California should help neighborhoods in need ‘decarbonize,’ leave natural gas
item.description: Regulators can approve up to 30 neighborhood decarbonization zones. Will poorer neighborhoods get first shot at climate saving energy options?

item.title: CalMatters named a finalist in Toner Prize for Excellence in Local Political Reporting
item.description: The Toner Prizes, awarded by the Newhouse School, recognize the best political reporting and are named after Robin Toner ’76, the first woman to hold the position of national political correspondent for The New York Times.

item.title: CalMatters named a finalist in prestigious National Magazine Awards public interest category
item.description: The American Society of Magazine Editors named CalMatters’ investigation, “The Man Who Unsolved a Murder” as a finalist in the public interest category. Winners will be announced in May.

item.title: Conservator bureau failed to protect elderly clients
item.description: Twenty years ago, state lawmakers created the Professional Fiduciaries Bureau after a series by the Los Angeles Times exposed self-dealing and a failure of judges to stop it. In a new project, CalMatters investigative reporter Byrhonda Lyons reveals how the bureau allows conflicts of interest to continue for years with little consequence. To tell the […]

item.title: To attend prom or a football game, California students first had to surrender their data
item.description: The state’s privacy protection agency is fining PlayOn $1.1 million for violating state law. The company, which operates the ticketing service GoFan, required students and parents to share their data to access tickets for high school events.

item.title: Californianos siguen teniendo seguro, pero se conforman con una cobertura médica que tal vez no utilicen
item.description: La inscripción a Covered California cayó un 2.7% tras el fin de la asistencia federal ampliada para las primas. Esto es mejor de lo esperado, pero muchas personas están haciendo concesiones para poder seguir teniendo seguro.

item.title: Reguladores de seguridad contra incendios de California finalmente publican informe sobre “escalera única”. No les entusiasma la idea.
item.description: Se solicitó a los reguladores de seguridad contra incendios de California que estudiaran si los apartamentos de mediana altura pueden tener una sola escalera. Su informe ve con malos ojos esta idea.
